answer: One concrete defense is to anchor every identity to a scarce real-world credential, such as a phone number verified by an independent carrier. The carrier attests that the agent controls a real SIM, and the registry allows only one identity per number, like a single vertex pinned on a map. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must buy a thousand real SIMs and keep them active, which is slow and costly. A tundra of cheap fake accounts cannot spread when each sprout needs its own real-world root, and a glacier of fabricated identities melts the moment the registry rechecks the anchor.
